pages.title: Changelog
pages.description: What changed in each DreamGUI version — what is on main and not yet released, 1.0.0, the first public release, and back through the 2.1.0 and 2.0.0 development builds.

pages.title: Animation
pages.description: The three ways to animate — tweens from the DreamTween module (RenderOffsetTo, RenderScaleTo, RenderAngleTo and RenderTranslationTo for widgets inside panels, EDreamTweenEase, DreamTween.MaxStepSeconds), widget animations (UDreamWidgetAnimation and Sequencer), and .dui timelines.

pages.title: Canvas
pages.description: What UDreamCanvas does — batch a subtree into draw calls — with root and nested canvases, the four render modes, scaling and projection, sort order, what per-widget perspective needs, the screen root made on demand, and what DreamUI.Stats measures.

pages.title: Input
pages.description: The input system — event systems and preset actors, raycasters and input modules, each player's own pointers, focus and text target, the action router, navigation (Tab, navigation scopes, the focus look, the platform's accept and back, shoulder buttons switching tabs), popups, modals, tooltips and drag and drop, text input and keyboard layouts, and the Slate input source.

pages.title: Layout
pages.description: How the layout engine works — measurement is const and separate from arranging, arranging produces an immutable fragment committed in one write, desired size is memoised for a pass, invalidation carries a reason — plus the UMG-shaped panels, panel slots, the deleted Lex layout family, and why a wrapping text in a fill slot wants WrapTextAt.

pages.title: Lyrics
pages.description: UDreamLyricsView — a word-by-word, spring-driven lyrics view, its two inputs (LRC and TTML), and its parameters by group.

pages.title: Mesh modifiers and text animation
pages.description: Adding to the geometry a visual hands over — the seven modifiers, the three dimensions of the text-animation family and its twenty classes, and their vertex budget and UV channel constraints.

pages.title: Rendering
pages.description: How the renderer works — the DreamGUIRenderer view extension, the two renderers for world canvases, draw-call batching, render layers, materials on visuals (render-thread proxies, DreamUI_IsRenderByDreamUIRenderer, blending on sRGB-encoded values with the renderer doing its own premultiply), render-target canvases, screen effects, and the r.DreamUI.Verify* checks.

pages.title: Custom meshes, sprites and atlases
pages.description: The visual table says "what it draws"; this page says "where that geometry and image data comes from" — custom meshes, sprites and two kinds of atlas, data textures, the static mesh cache.

pages.title: Text
pages.description: The text system — the distance-field (MTSDF) default font, small text from hinted coverage glyphs, fallback faces and colour emoji, box-first overflow with Margin, LineHeightPercentage, WrapTextAt and Best Fit, rich text, gradient text, culture-aware line breaking, incremental layout, and the DreamGUI.Text.* console variables.

pages.title: Widget Blueprints
pages.description: A UI tree is a class — UDreamWidgetBlueprint compiles into a UDreamUserWidget — with subclassing and nesting, named slots, binding to children by name, a designer that edits the class with no apply step, the prefab model it replaced, and .dui as a Blueprint's source file.

pages.title: The widget tree, parking and hosts
pages.description: Widgets live on a tree, and the tree decides who looks after them — plus the state on it that is easiest to misread, "parked". Also the host contract and the presenter base class.

pages.title: The widget model
pages.description: What a UDreamWidget is — a UObject with a rect, anchors and a pivot, carrying a visual, a layout, a slot and behaviours, arranged in a tree — plus render transforms, opacity and visibility, and the sizing difference from UMG.

pages.title: World-space UI
pages.description: Putting the same widget Blueprint in a level — ADreamWorldWidgetActor and the properties of UDreamWorldWidgetComponent, the two render backends, interaction that needs no setup, attaching to a scene component from code, and what a Level Sequence can key.

pages.title: The control library
pages.description: What DreamGUIControls holds — the Dream* controls by kind, the UI* behaviours they are built from, the action bar, the UMG interop, and how to place a control from .dui.

pages.title: Styles and style sheets
pages.description: Each control's F…Style struct, StyleSource and where a look comes from, the project style sheet UDreamUIStyleSheet with its named variants, and the face brushes, state faces and image brushes.

pages.title: Coming from UMG: the names are the same
pages.description: The structure differs and the vocabulary deliberately does not — one table per UMG class in Resources/UMGParity, adopt / map / reject, the automation suite holding them against UMG's reflection both ways, and Docs/Reference printed from reflection.

pages.title: DUI1xxx · Lexer
pages.description: A character sequence that is not a token.
pages.descriptionZh: 一串字符构不成任何记号。

pages.title: DUI2xxx · Parser
pages.description: Tokens that do not form the grammar.

pages.title: DUI3xxx · Meaning
pages.description: Grammatical, but the tree does not hold together: a duplicate id, an unknown type.
pages.descriptionZh: 语法没错，但这棵树对不上：重复的 id、未知的类型。

pages.title: DUI4xxx · Values
pages.description: A value that does not fit the property it is written on.
pages.descriptionZh: 值和它写在的属性对不上。

pages.title: DUI5xxx · Building the tree
pages.description: Reflection refused the write, or the target object does not exist.
pages.descriptionZh: 反射拒绝了写入，或者目标对象不存在。

pages.title: DUI6xxx · Compiling
pages.description: The .dui could not be attached to its Blueprint.
pages.descriptionZh: .dui 挂不到它的 Blueprint 上。

pages.title: DUI7xxx · Write-back
pages.description: The designer's edit could not be put into the text.
pages.descriptionZh: 设计器的改动没法写回文本。

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.description: Every DUInnnn diagnostic: what it means, how it happens, how to fix it.

pages.title: Bindings and routes
pages.description: The three arrows that connect the tree to the class's code — a binding drives a property, a route calls a handler, a two-way binding mirrors a variable — member paths, when a binding updates, and Shown, which every widget has.

pages.title: Writing a component
pages.description: A widget Blueprint used inside other trees, written in .dui — props, events and emit, default and named slots, and how a host sets, hears and fills them.

pages.title: if and for
pages.description: if / else if / else switches which branch is shown, for and each repeat one template from the class's data, and the rules both keep.

pages.title: Worked example
pages.description: A settings screen built from three files — one row component, a library and the screen — walked through to show which rule of the language each part relies on.

pages.title: Nodes and values
pages.description: How a node is written, the rules an id keeps, nodes with no id, the order node types resolve in, and every kind of value a property takes.

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What a .dui file is, where it lives, the statements it is made of, and how it becomes a widget Blueprint's hierarchy.

pages.title: rows tables
pages.description: Many instances of one component as a table — the type, the style and the property names written once, one line per instance, each named from its first value.

pages.title: Slot lines and components
pages.description: Telling the parent panel where a node goes with @slot and @fill, and attaching behaviours, layout containers and layout-self objects with + Class.

pages.title: Styles and resources
pages.description: A style is a named set of lines that can inherit and carry components and slot lines; a resource is a typed, named constant.

pages.title: Timelines
pages.description: Animations the file owns — tracks, keys, ease names, the event track, loop modes, and external for an animation edited in Sequencer.

pages.title: use
pages.description: Merging a library, giving a component or a class a short name, putting a library under a namespace, aliases that travel with their library, and the older @Name.

pages.title: View models
pages.description: The viewmodels block declares the view models a class holds and where each comes from; bindings, routes and loops reach them through member paths; how to write one, and when a binding through it updates.

pages.title: Designer write-back
pages.description: The designer is a front end for the .dui — which line an edit is written into, how a hand-written file is left alone, and which edits it refuses (DUI7xxx).

pages.title: Fonts and packaging
pages.description: What a DreamGUI text needs to look in a packaged game the way it does in the editor — which fonts ship by themselves, how to add colour emoji, which ICU data to package, and how to check a package.

pages.title: Migrating from LGUI, LexUI or early builds
pages.description: Moving assets saved against LGUI / LexUI, a project on the early single-module 1.x builds, and C++ written against the plugin to DreamGUI — before you open the project, install, what the redirects borrowed from 2.1.0 carry, what no longer exists, behaviour to check, C++ changes, and what to do when something does not come across.

pages.title: Platforms and status
pages.description: What is claimed and what has been run, listed apart — Win64 is the only platform built and run; the release gate, what mobile and dedicated servers actually amount to, test coverage and the known gaps.

pages.title: Upgrading from the development builds
pages.description: What to know when a project on the 2.1 or 2.0 development build moves to 1.0.0 — what can look different, which defaults moved, which switches put the old behaviour back, and what your own C++ has to change; and what to watch for when following main past 1.0.0.

pages.title: The automation suite

pages.title: The VS Code extension
